title: Superordinate Objectives

html:
When we ask "what objective does the brain optimize?", the most productive answer is not a single scalar but a stack of drives, constraints, and learned goals layered across phylogeny, physiology, development, and culture. Evolution does not hand the organism an explicit utility function; it bakes objective priors into anatomy and plasticity rules by making survival-critical variables (glucose, temperature, hydration, tissue damage, social inclusion, etc.) matter to circuitry. Day-to-day behavior then looks like partially observed control over hidden bodily and environmental states: keep the organism inside a viability manifold (hard constraints) while opportunistically improving future prospects (soft preferences) under time/energy/computation limits. Formal homeostatic RL makes this explicit: seeking "reward" is equivalent to defending physiological variables, and even classic temporal discounting can be derived as the shortest path back to setpoints in homeostatic space 1. This framing dissolves the apparent tension between "reward maximization" and "survival": rewards are not arbitrary hedonic bonuses but proxy signals for restoring viability, and the effective discount factor reflects the dynamics of physiological drift (how fast the system departs from setpoints) rather than being a free parameter. The homeostatic state-space model makes physiological reward explicit (Figure). An active-inference proposal supplies a complementary generative-model diagram (Figure) 2.

This section describes the objectives that most fundamentally guide the evolution, development, and everyday operation of the human brain (superordinate objectives). These forces determine the curriculum that emerges across evolutionary and individual timescales. Later sections (especially the "Dense, Chronological Account of Human Learning" section) will enumerate the concrete, domain-specific objectives (e.g. "navigate to the kitchen", "perform addition", "earn a degree") and the sequence of training recipes that optimize against them. A compact taxonomy of superordinate objectives:

Viability regulation: keep interoceptive variables in safe ranges (homeostasis/allostasis; pain/avoidance as constraint signals).

Epistemic control: reduce uncertainty that matters for control (hidden state, dynamics, parameters, other agents).

Control / option value: maintain and expand reachable futures (controllability/empowerment; skill acquisition as channel expansion).

Social-normative value: status, belonging, attachment, reputation, fairness, identity; internalized norms as learned constraints.

Cognitive economy: trade decision quality vs time/energy/computation (bounded rationality/resource rationality).
